earlier_scan.source_named: Wilson, W. A. A. 2007. Guinea Languages of the Atlantic Group: Description and Internal Classification. Frankfurt: Peter Lang (covers Landuma); also Wilson 1962, 'Temne, Landuma and the Baga languages'
earlier_scan.note: Print descriptions of Landuma exist (Wilson; Sumbatova's Russian-language verb studies) but none reachable online

sources.citation: Grambank (Hübler coder), Landoma land1256; sources Sumbatova 1999 and Sumbatova 2012.
sources.note: No stress features; only confirms the two Russian sources used for grammatical coding.

sources.citation: Sumbatova, Nina & Valentin Vydrin. 2021. N-initial nouns in Landuma and their counterparts in Mande. Journal of Language Relationship 19(1-2): 136-151. DOI 10.31826/jlr-2021-191-212.
sources.note: Section 1 (p. 136) gives the vowel and consonant inventory (Table 1) and notes an IPA-based transcription; no mention of stress, accent, tone or prosody anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: only Mande tone references).

sources.citation: Sumbatova, N. R. 2018. Osnovanija imennykh klassifikacij: ot semantiki do fonologii. Voprosy Jazykoznanija 2018(6): 7-30. DOI 10.31857/S0373658X0002018-8.
sources.note: Landing page and abstract read at vja.ruslang.ru (abstract: describes the Landuma agreement system determined by the phonological structure of the controller noun); no PDF offered; nothing on stress in the abstract.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and bibliography for land1256 (22 entries in local BIB_BY_LANG, incl. Rogers & Bryant 2012 dictionary, Sumbatova 2003, 2012, Wilson 1962, Dalby 1965, Houis 1950).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; no phonology-typed reference; Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are Itkine & Soumbatova 1994 (4 pp., agreement) and wordlists.
No phonology section; cites Wilson 2007 only.

sources.note: The only published description of Landuma phonology by a fieldworker; Google Books index snippet shows a Tone subsection with Landuma in Table 83; the abstract of the underlying survey says tonal systems were found in every Guinea Atlantic language except Fula and Diola. Would settle tone vs stress for Landuma.
